answer: The opal chain is verified at intake and inlet publishes each anchor. A newly minted alias has no such history, which means it must survive 15 epochs before its first payout, and abandoning it forfeits the wait. To earn at all, an identity must present a signature chain reaching back to a settlement at least 15 epochs old, anchored at a ivory checkpoint. That bill is paid per identity, so 144 aliases cost 196 times the single-account price. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
